title: Google Antigravity adds Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5
key_facts: Google's Antigravity coding tool (its agentic IDE, built after the roughly $2.4 billion Windsurf licensing and hiring deal) now lists Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in its model picker, per Google's model documentation.

Access is limited to paying Google AI Pro ($19.99 a month) and Ultra ($99.99 and $199.99) subscribers; a trial Pro plan, free, AI Plus and Enterprise tiers do not get them, according to the documentation and pricing reported by CloudZero.
Antigravity had been running the older Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 even after Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5 on 22 Sep and Sonnet 5.5 on 28 Sep 2026; the 4.6 models are scheduled for removal on 2 Nov.
Google has not announced the change in a blog post or changelog; the model page is the only confirmation so far.
Antigravity's default is Gemini 3.1 Pro with a 1 million token context; it also offers OpenAI's GPT-OSS 120B, all billed through a Google account.
quote_evidence: Google's Antigravity coding platform has quietly added Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 to its model picker, but only for paying Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.
Google's model documentation says a trial Pro subscription doesn't unlock the new Claude models.
Google's model page confirms the addition, while the changelog still does not call out either model.
why_it_matters_hint: Google keeps its coding tool a place where a rival's newest models compete with Gemini, which changes how teams buy AI coding capacity (one Google bill instead of separate API accounts).
event_date: not stated; article 3 Oct 2026, change found in Google documentation
notes: Single outlet reading Google's documentation; no Google statement. Exact date of the change not given. Page contains unrelated promotional snippets ignored.
